atlas_n_mission.challenge: how does a program's `open` foreign call reach Miri's Unix file shim (shims/unix/fs.rs `open`) -- which path does Atlas observe?
atlas_n_mission.answer: E18 and E19 alike: NO_PATH_OBSERVED, UNKNOWN. The true path is emulate_foreign_item_inner (foreign_items.rs:111) -> `this.open(path_raw, flag, varargs)` -> EvalContextExt::open (fs.rs:404), where `this` is `self.eval_context_mut()`, of the external type InterpCx<MiriMachine>; an unseen inherent method of that type could win the method probe over Miri's extension traits, so Atlas leaves the call unresolved by name (the G167 external-declaration boundary) -- the oracle holds 26 foreign_items -> fs edges, all through such `this.` calls

cases.question: does `use crate::*` in a module of a crate whose root globs an external crate make every glob-provided name unknowable?
cases.ground_truth: no: a name the root binds by an item or a named import is the root's (named shadows glob), and another glob binding it differently would be an ambiguity error (E0659)
cases.atlas_n: yes: 2,106 path calls in 90 modules withheld
cases.atlas_n_plus_1: the certain names resolve (withheld 2,385 -> 1,767); root names bound only through its external glob stay withheld

cases.question: does `use TerminationInfo::*` inside a block of diagnostics.rs resolve?
cases.ground_truth: it does in rustc, but the enclosing function globs InterpErrorKind::* and UndefinedBehaviorInfo::* (external enums) first, whose variants Atlas cannot see and could shadow `TerminationInfo` in that block

implementation.mechanism_vs_implementation: nothing of Miri is absorbed: its crate, indexed by rust-analyzer, falsified one over-conservative Atlas rule; the fix follows Rust's own shadowing and ambiguity rules (named shadows glob; glob-glob is an error when used; only an item may shadow a glob), not any Miri code
implementation.change: adapter semantic::rust::resolve: Module::items_open (open before import resolution, or with no fixed point), Entry::certain (a glob name its source binds by an item or named import, or by a certain glob of a module not open), uncertain_entry replacing the four glob-in-uncertain-module checks (ADR 0086)
implementation.falsification: regression test a_certain_name_survives_a_glob_of_an_open_module (the miri shape) and the reworked an_open_scope_never_falls_through_and_trusts_only_its_certain_globs; 4 mutants killed (nothing certain; certainty through an open source -- the first version of the change, caught by the test; items_open ignored; items_open never set)
